# Repository agent skills

This repository keeps shared agent skills in `.agents/skills/` and records their
sources and content hashes in `skills-lock.json`. Install project skills from the
repository root with
`npx skills add <source> --skill <name> --agent codex --agent cursor --copy`.
Using `--copy` preserves the repository's existing checked-in layout.

Cursor loads project skills reliably from `.cursor/skills/`. This repo keeps a
symlink at `.cursor/skills` → `.agents/skills` so Codex and Cursor share one
checked-in copy. Without that path, Cursor may treat `.agents/skills` entries as
rules instead of invocable skills (`/skill-name`).

input.command: git status --short .cursor docs/agent-skills.md; git check-ignore -v .cursor/skills 2>&1 || true; ls -la .cursor/skills

content.text:
Done. Your skills lived under `.agents/skills/` (Codex layout). Cursor treats that path unreliably — they often show up as **Rules**, not invocable **Skills**.

**Fix:** `.cursor/skills` → symlink to `.agents/skills` (one copy, both agents). Docs in `docs/agent-skills.md` updated to match.

**Try it:** reload the window (`Developer: Reload Window`), then type `/coding-standards` or `/code-review` in Agent chat. They should appear under Settings → Rules → Skills.

Say if you want this symlink committed.
